rows.text: Today @TheLancet published our AMIE study with @BIDMC_Medicine, the first prospective study of patient-facing conversational diagnostics in a real clinic. AMIE is a research system people can chat with before doctors appointments. Testing AMIE outside the lab with real urgent care patients showed how technology can help gather medical histories safely. Clinicians reported that the summaries helped them prepare for visits in 75% of cases and influenced their approach to care in more than half. AMIE’s differential diagnoses also matched the doctors’ final diagnoses 90% of the time giving clinici

rows.author: Google
rows.name: Google
rows.text: Our medical research system, AMIE, is the first patient-facing conversational diagnostic tool of its kind to be studied prospectively in a real-world clinical setting. In a study, published today in @TheLancet, we found that when patients chatted with AMIE before an in-person appointment, the interaction built their confidence and helped them organize their thoughts. And physicians who reviewed the information from the patient conversation got more time back to focus on collaborative care and shared decision-making instead of digging through data.

rows.text: 🇺🇸 Peter Schiff sees something in this stock market that has only happened twice in the last century. In 1973 and again around the dot-com bubble, market gains became this concentrated in so few stocks. Both times, the S&P eventually fell close to 50%. “Every time you get to a situation that you know is extreme and has a history of ending in a disaster, everybody always says, ‘Yes, but this time it’s different.’” Schiff’s concern is that America is now making the same bet again, only this time the magic word is AI. rows.author: MarioNawfal
rows.name: Mario Nawfal
rows.text: When Cybertruck becomes the getaway car for astronauts, you know the job is serious. NASA has certified Cybertruck as the emergency egress vehicle for SpaceX crews, parked near the pad and ready to move fast if something goes wrong. If suited crew need to get out fast, instant torque, quick acceleration and protection all matter a lot. Astronauts can slide down, get in, and clear the area without waiting on engine start-up or slower heavy vehicles. Cybertruck is pretty well suited for rocket-adjacent problems. @Tesla @SpaceX @Cybertruck / Writer: Annette, Designer: Janné
